contents.text: The heart has four hollow sections, called chambers, which are surrounded by the thick wall of the heart.

alternativeText.text: A diagram of the heart, showing how blood flows through the chambers

textContent.text: The heart wall is made up mainly of two types of tissue. Cardiac muscle tissue expands and contracts, and connective tissue provides support.

The heart's chambers open and close to pump blood through the heart and to the body. When the heart wall around a chamber expands, the hollow chamber opens and fills with blood. When the wall contracts, the chamber squeezes closed and pumps the blood out.

textContent.text: The heart is part of an organ system called the circulatory system, which also includes the blood and the blood vessels. The blood and the smallest blood vessels are tissues. Larger blood vessels are organs.

All the parts of the circulatory system work together to carry out its function. The heart pumps blood through blood vessels, which extend throughout the body. As blood travels through the blood vessels, it carries nutrients to different parts of the body and carries away waste products.

explanationText.text: Organ systems are made up of many cells. The cells can make up tissues, and the tissues can make up organs. These parts all work together as an organ system to do a certain job.

content.text: Organ systems work independently from the rest of the body.

explanationText.text: Organ systems work with the rest of the body, not independently from it. For example, the circulatory system has blood vessels throughout the body. Blood travels through these blood vessels, carrying nutrients and waste products around the body.

content.text: The smallest and simplest systems within organ systems are the organs.

contents.text: The human body is a system of many organ systems that work together.

alternativeText.text: An image of Blood vessels lining air sacs in the lungs

textContent.text: For example, the circulatory system works closely with the respiratory system. One of the respiratory system's functions is to bring oxygen from the air into the body.

To carry out this function, the respiratory system uses several organs, including the lungs. In the lungs, air travels to small air sacs, where oxygen is transferred from the air to the blood. This oxygen-rich blood travels through blood vessels to the heart and then to the rest of the body. The body's cells need the oxygen in the blood to carry out cell processes.

textContent.text: For example, the circulatory system works closely with the respiratory system. One of the respiratory system's functions is to bring oxygen from the air into the body.

To carry out this function, the respiratory system uses several organs, including the lungs. In the lungs, air travels to small air sacs, where oxygen is transferred from the air to the blood. This oxygen-rich blood travels through blood vessels to the heart and then to the rest of the body. The body's cells need the oxygen in the blood to carry out cell processes.
